Got a really good history of this competition and that’s where we want to challenge ourselves and test ourselves. you know, we’ve worked hard to be here. We want a reaction You know, we haven’t had the results that we wanted, that we expected. Fine margins in some of them games and it can go both ways, but the reality is exactly where we are now and this is a fresh opportunity.Continue reading...

item.title: Barrios strikes after 53 seconds as Atlético pile misery on 10-man Manchester United
item.author: Sid Lowe at the Riyadh Air Metropolitano
item.content:encoded: Michael Carrick had seen it in his players, he said, but no one else can. Not so far in the Premier League, where they have suffered their worst start in 40 years, and not here in Madrid, where Manchester United’s head coach insisted they would embrace the challenge. The reaction was coming, he promised; he had looked at them and was sure of it. Instead, they were a goal down after just 53 seconds and all that came was the old familiar sting, that early opener from Pablo Barrios and a second from Ademola Lookman condemning them to another defeat.So much for a reaction, a rebellion: in their place a kind of resignation, a sense that maybe this is just United’s reality: a game that began badly, did not get very much better, and finished even worse. True, the result could have been different, Bryan Mbeumo unable to convert two first-half chances while Bruno Fernandes struck the bar and put an opportunity wide, but that did not diminish the feeling that something is really wrong. It may even have deepened it.Continue reading...

item.title: Gravel Burn introduces 'new dimension' of teams classification at October stage race while schedules revealed for BWR and Grasshopper series - Gravel Bits
item.author: jackie.tyson@futurenet.com (Jackie Tyson)
item.content:encoded: The second edition of the seven-day Gravel Burn gravel stage race in South Africa, October 25-31, introduces a teams classification with points to determine standings and prizes. It will be the first such classification recognition at a gravel stage race.Trade teams of three to four riders, as well as alliances of independent riders, will be eligible for the new classification. The top three riders from each team will earn points that will contribute to the daily standings. Organisers developed the format in collaboration with several individuals, including pro road and gravel veteran Peter Stetina of Canyon x DT Swiss ATR and Adam Hansen, president of the CPA (Cyclistes Professionnels Associés), both having participated in last year’s inaugural race."This innovation provides another dimension to the racing and also rewards the riders’ efforts and the teams’ investment," said race founder Kevin Vermaak. "Independent ‘privateer’ racers formed the foundation of professional gravel racing, adding to the ‘freedom’ and charm of gravel. We recognise that the emergence of ‘superteams’ is a threat to that. That’s why we opened the Teams Classification to all to help level the playing field, where they may form ad-hoc teams to compete with the more formal outfits.”Canyon x DT Swiss ATR will field a women's team led by former Unbound Gravel 200 winner Carolin Schiff. They will also start two men's teams, one led by former US gravel champion Bradyn Lange. Scott-SRAM will have one team in each division, the women's team including Life Time Grand Prix contender Alexis Skarda and the men's team with Filippo Colombo, who won the UCI Gravel World Series Ceder race in February. Toyota Specialized Imbuko will have two men's teams with all-South African rosters, while Mattia De Marchi will lead a three-rider men's team for The Grip.The solo race remains the foundation of Nedbank Gravel Burn, with a $150,000 US prize purse split equally between the pro women and pro men categories, including daily payouts to the top 3 and overall top 10. Gravel Burn is a full-service stage race in the Eastern Cape of South Africa, covering 750 kilometres and 8,500 metres of elevation gain.Among the debutants for individuals are two-time Marathon MTB world champion Henrique Avancini of Brazil, multi-time Japanese XCO mountain bike champion Kohei Yamamoto, as well as 18-year road pro and a former Cape Epic winner Jakob Fuglsang.Last year's men's champion Matt Beers returns, as well as runner-up Simon Pellaud. Women's champion Axelle Dubau-Prevot will defend her title, lining up against third-placed Hayley Preen.Five events have been confirmed for the Belgian Waffle Ride schedule next year, with a new Colorado event taking shape. Registration opened October 13 for a quartet of US events spread from March to September, while Mexico takes place in late November. The sequence of events remains the same, opening in Arizona in early March and then moving to Southern California on May 2, the 16th season for the signature event. The Utah event in Cedar City shifts from June to mid-May, and the Bozeman, Montana event then moves from June to mid-September. Event organisers Monuments of Gravel are looking to fill the summer with a new event in Colorado, though the location has not been named and it is not known if this will be part of the series. The final ride in the BWR mixed-surface collection will again be held in Mexico on November 21, but is not part of the elite series."What began as one questionable idea in San Diego has now carried us through more than 42 events, with a remarkable collection of riders, partners and friends giving it far more life than we could have imagined," noted BWR founder Michael Marckx.The Quad-Tripel Crown of Gravel series has been offered for several seasons across the US-based collection of events, and will return with the best three of four races determining elite winners. A usual suspect in the series has been Utah, but it may be a standalone race in 2027, according to organisers, and could become a UCI Gravel World Series qualifier.Belgian Waffle Ride schedule 2027September 18 - BWR MontanaThe race schedule for the 2027 Grasshopper Adventure Series, now in its 30th year, was released with five races in northern California. The opener takes place at Low Gap on January 31, a 59-mile gravel event with 95% dirt tracks in Ukiah, and culminates at Ukiah Mendo Epic on May 23, a 70-mile mixed-terrain adventure in the same area. The middle of the schedule includes the classic mixed-terrain Huffmaster on February 28, the road and climbing-heavy King Ridge on March 20 and the gravel-singletrack challenge of Jackson Forest on April 10.Registration is open, and a series pass for all five events is $675, plus fees, with individual races at $155 each. Prices go up after November 30, two months before the opener.Last year, Jen Tavé (SpeedBlock-Terún Pro Cycling) and Cassius Anderson (Marin Service Course) secured the overall titles for elite divisions in the five-race Grasshopper Series.Grasshopper Adventure Series schedule 2027January 31 - Low Gap at Ukiah, CaliforniaFebruary 28 - Huffmaster at Maxwell, CaliforniaMarch 20 - King Ridge at Guerneville, CaliforniaApril 10 - Jackson Forest at Casper, CaliforniaMay 23 - Ukiah Mendo Epic at Ukiah, California

item.title: Eneco Tour: Jakob Söderqvist secures leader's jersey as fastest rider in nighttime prologue at The Hague
item.author: jackie.tyson@futurenet.com (Jackie Tyson)
item.content:encoded: Jakob Söderqvist (Lidl-Trek) won the prologue Tuesday night in The Hague to take the first leader's jersey of the Eneco Tour. Sweden's time trial champion was the third-to-last rider on the 3.1km course and posted a winning time of 3 minutes, 32 seconds. A surprising time just seven-tenths of a second slower gave 23-year old Wessel Mouris (Unibet Rose Rockets) second place. Last year's stage race GC winner Christophe Laporte (Visma-Lease a Bike) was third, 1.4 seconds behind the winner."These prologues are so much adrenaline, and you're really in a hot box in the end and super on your nerves when you cross the finish line," Söderqvist said to TV cameras at the finish. He had no idea how tight the times were, and said "oh, better buy a lottery ticket then" when told his time was half a second better than Wessel Mouris."I had a pleasure to have a couple of days in orange also last year, and to be back here with good enough shape to start it even better."For a while it looked like both Mouris brothers would grab podium spots, with Michiel Mouris (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) going second to his brother. Then the final four riders in the final wave shook the standings on scorching rides.Great Britain's time trial champion Ethan Hayter (Soudal-QuickStep), who won the prologue last year, knocked Michiel Mouris down a spot with a faster time by 1 second. Then Laporte and Söderqvist dispatched the 19-year-old to fifth place, Hayter going fourth, and one brother on the podium. The recreated Tour of Holland, now Eneco Tour, made a return last year after a 21-year absence from the UCI calendar, and the composition of two time trials and four road stages was replicated for the 2026 edition. However, the twist this year was that all six days of racing integrated racing for pro women, formerly the Ladies Tour of Holland. The blend of staggered start times and similar routes using circuits began with the Prologue. The action began Tuesday with a unique process for the 3.1km prologue - waves of women and men sharing the same course. The first 28 women took the start in The Hague at one-minute intervals followed by a five-minute break and then the first 28 men hit the course with the same spacing. This pattern for alternating waves was repeated, with a total of 88 women and 88 men on the start list, the early riders seeing the sun setting while the city course became illuminated by street lamps in the darkness.The start ramp was inside the Sportcampus Zuiderpark multi-functional arena, Robbe Claeys (Volkerwessels Cycling) the first men's rider down the ramp at 18:34 local time for a quick lap around the park, and setting the standard at 3:52. Nils Eekhoff (Picnic PostNL) took over the hot seat just six riders later with 3:47, and then was dispatched by Joeri Schaper (Soudal-QuickStep) who went four seconds faster. The second wave of 30 riders started with Thor Verleysen (Volkerwessels Cycling). Eight riders later, Hartthijs De Vries (Unibet Rose Rockets) flew across the course as the first rider to go under three minutes, 40 seconds, posting 3:39. He was nearly knocked off the hot seat by Victor Campenaerts (Visma-Lease a Bike), who came through six-tenths of a second slower.It was De Vries' teammate Thomáš Kopecký who then took over with 3:37. He held the best time as only Pepijn Reinderink (Soudal-QuickStep) came within one second from the next six riders completing the middle wave.The final wave saw 23-year-old Wessel Mouris grab the lead in a time of 3:33. The TV camera showed him smiling broadly when his brother, Michiel Mouris almost took the spotlight, going just two seconds slower. The brothers, however, were one-two with 15 riders to go.The last three riders featured Söderqvist, Laporte and New Zealand TT champion Finn Fischer-Black (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe). Söderqvist stormed around the circuit for the best time, with Laporte getting a podium spot, but Fisher-Black coming up short in sixth.After the prologue, stage 1 takes place in Ede with a flat 40-kilometre circuit that the men tackle three times and women twice. item.title: Eneco Tour Women: Lieke Nooijen dominates prologue for first race leader's jersey
item.author: kirsten.frattini@futurenet.com (Kirsten Frattini)
item.content:encoded: Lieke Nooijen (Visma-Lease a Bike) secured the prologue victory and took the first leader's jersey at the Eneco Tour Women. The Dutch rider covered the 3.1km course with the fastest time of 3:51, beating her compatriots Charlotte Kool (Fenix-Premier Tech) and Lonneke Uneken (VolkerWessels) by eight seconds in The Hague.Nooijen started her time trial in the third of three waves, surpassing both Kool, who posted the early benchmark and had sat in the hot seat since the opening wave, and Uneken to take the day's spoils.The Dutch road race national champion now leads the overall classification heading into stage 1 in Ede on Wednesday."I'm super happy with this victory. I've worked really hard towards this, so it's great to win such a short prologue by eight seconds," she said."I went full gas from the start and managed to maintain my speed throughout. These short efforts really suit me, and that paid off today."This year all six days of racing will integrate stages for pro women, formerly the Ladies Tour of Holland, and for pro men, formerly the NIBC Tour of Holland, with staggered start times and similar routes.The action began Tuesday with a unique process for the 3.1km prologue - waves of women and men sharing the same course. The first 30 women took the start in The Hague at one-minute intervals, followed by a five-minute break, and then the first 30 men hit the course with the same spacing. This alternating-wave pattern repeated, with a total of 88 women and 88 men on the start list.During the first wave of the women's prologue, Kool posted the fastest time of 3:59, averaging nearly 17kph across the 3.1km course. Femke Markus (SD Worx-Protime) and Margaux Vigié (Visma-Lease a Bike) were both three seconds slower in second and third placeHowever, the second wave started about thirty minutes with three riders slotting in behind Kool; Sandrine Tas (Lotto Intermarché Ladies) stormed into the runner's-up spot just a fraction of a second slower, Maud Rijnbeek (VolkerWessels) a two seconds back and Letizia Borghesi (AG Insurance-Soudal) at three seconds back, bumping Markus and Vigié out of the top three.The third wave on course would decide the final top placings of the prologue, and while Kool was the day's leader for much of this event, her time was encroached upon by Uneken, who stormed across the finish line with the second-fastest time of the day, a fraction of a second slower than Kool.But there would be one faster rider on course to surpass them both, with Nooijen putting a stamp on the prologue with the victory and the event's first leader's jersey.Lieke Nooijen (Team Visma | Lease a item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.author: Guardian sport
item.content:encoded: Manchester City unrepentant in victory, Spurs make progress of a sort and Noni Madueke meets the momentThe manner of Manchester City’s victory at Liverpool was an article of both vindication and vilification. Those gleefully wielding inflatable bananas in the Anfield away end could thumb their noses. Why not enjoy the dances of defiance until the music stops? The same went for City players, asked to perform under the darkest of clouds, able to focus, at last, on football, rather than legal argument and uncertain futures. Beyond City, the sight of a club found guilty of 100-plus charges laying waste to such rivals as Liverpool was deeply uncomfortable. The Premier League season and product are badly damaged until the matter is somehow resolved. What happened at Anfield should double the haste for a resolution. Chants of “cheat” whenever City players, the game already won, slipped the ball around, are bound to be repeated at other stadiums. Enzo Maresca has described his club’s plight as “noise” but his team’s victory did absolutely nothing to turn the volume down. Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester United and Spurs come back to reality as City saga offers brief distraction | John Brewin
item.author: John Brewin at Old Trafford
item.content:encoded: Manchester City’s rule breaches have dominated headlines and shifted focus from both clubs’ self-inflicted woundsTurning back the clock is impossible. Up in the Stretford End’s middle tier, the ticker had returned, a retouching job to “51 years” invoiced for the pertinent sum of £114. The Manchester City that existed before the Abu Dhabi project won their last trophy in 1976. Questionable maths is perhaps not confined to the Etihad’s accounts department, though Manchester United’s support must get their kicks where they can.Should City’s fall from grace be fully confirmed by the appeals and sanctions process, there is nothing in the way of irrefutable evidence of United’s former supremacy being restored. How United fans would love to return to 2008, when Michael Carrick was a key cog in Sir Alex Ferguson’s team of European champions. Instead, the autumn of 2026 brings a familiar swell of doubt, another manager dragged towards the meat grinder. It will be 40 years next month since Ferguson was appointed. A draw made United’s start to their league campaign the worst since then. The Carrick bounce has come to a standstill.Continue reading...
